label: static-inference
claim: The X-M1 1.50 boot records, loaders and decoded images target an ARMv7-R core with a PMSAv7 MPU and VFPv3-D16, matching Cortex-R4F: code programs PMSA MPU region registers (c6,c2,0 then c6,c1,{4,0,2}), never accesses TTBR0/TTBR1/TTBCR or DACR, writes Cortex-R4/R5 implementation-defined c15,c5,0 and c9,c1,1, uses ARMv7 DSB/ISB and cache-ID registers, saves only d0-d15 in the VFP context switch, uses ARMv6T2 MOVW/MOVT throughout and contains no A32 SDIV/UDIV. The native runner now emulates Unicorn 2.1.4 Cortex-R5F, the closest available model, and rejects R5F-only A32 divide.
scope: Static inference, 2026-10-03, from permissive whole-image LLVM A32 linear-sweep listings of the exact 1.50 boot records (payload 0x40048/0x50048), loaders (0x40000/0xd0000), plain image (0x01100000) and decoded id4/id5, with the cited sequences read in context. Emulator model properties read from Unicorn 2.1.4 source. Independently reviewed and corrections verified (CPU-REVIEW-01).
sources: Sibling lead only: https://github.com/tiredboffin/fffw/wiki/EXR-II-CPU; FujiHack wiki https://wiki.fujihack.org/todo/ (unsourced ARM11 note, other bodies)
commands: devenv shell -- llvm-objcopy -I binary -O elf32-littlearm --rename-section .data=.text,alloc,load,code,contents IMAGE.bin IMAGE.elf

devenv shell -- llvm-objdump -d --triple=armv7a-none-eabi --mattr=+neon,+vfp4,+mp,+virtualization,+hwdiv-arm,+trustzone IMAGE.elf; tallies of p15 MCR/MRC by register and of SDIV/UDIV over each whole listing
limitations: MIDR and the other c0,c0-c7 ID registers are never read; core identity and revision are unobserved, and an R5F whose code avoids A32 divide also fits the bytes.

Linear-sweep listings include data words. Three id5 data words (0x4a4b28, 0x4a67dc, 0x4ac1f0) decode as conditional SDIV, and remaining CRn=c2/c3 decodes in id4/id5/img6 are data or MCR2/MRC2; code claims rest on in-context sequences.
The MPU layout alone is shared with PMSAv6, and the fault-address reads exist under VMSA too; v7 rests on DSB/ISB and the cache-ID registers.
Independent review CPU-REVIEW-01 re-derived every table row from the bytes, confirmed the conclusion and verified the corrections; it covered no Thumb regions or hardware.
Thumb use, exception/mode setup, ABI and float conventions remain open; no target execution or camera observation.
Unicorn's R5F differs from an R4F in A32 divide, multiprocessing ID, ID values, a 16-region MPU and dummy TCM/cache registers; docs/principles.md forbids depending on them.

claim: On X-M1 1.50 the boot records load neither image 5 nor the plain image. Image 4 loads both, from its flashloader task 0x73b3a0 (created by 0x73ac7c, mailbox 0x3c): case 0 at 0x73b4ac calls 0x6a96c0, which takes segment-table id 5 (entry at payload 0x14013c: load 0x00bf1a00, size 0x4f1e60, flash 0x002c0000/0x002e0000), reads logical blocks 0x16-0x2c into staging 0x43e40000 and feeds the 0xfff43000 engine, delivering 0x00bf1a00; case 3 at 0x73b554 calls 0x6a9844, which takes id 6 (entry at payload 0x140160: flash 0x005a0000/0x00360000) and reads blocks 0x2d-0x47 straight to the destination word at 0x61c1a8 = 0x01100000 with no engine and no CPU copy loop. Image 4 also carries a relocated engine driver (0x6843c8, 0x684308, wrappers 0x684760/0x6847d8/0x684828/0x684880) that forms the register addresses with movw/movt pairs, which the earlier literal-only scan missed.
scope: X-M1 1.50 decoded image 4 plus the preserved payload segment table and record headers; host-only, spot-checked from the bytes at every named address on 2026-10-07; the installed body shows both images resident (E-RAM-PROBE-150)
limitations: Static inference: no load was observed in progress, and the task and command sequence is read from the image, not executed.
The companion core's part in any of the loads is not assigned.

Entry 6's load, size and bss words are dead in this build: 0x6a9844 is its only reader and uses only the flash fields and the extent descriptor, and the loader stages never call the entry getter; why the vendor table repeats entry 5's values is not derivable from the images.

The staging constants are hard-coded per caller (boot 0x42e40000, id-5 loader 0x43e40000), image 4, 5 and 6 code uses 0x42e40000 elsewhere, and no code derives either constant, so the choice is not explained by the images.
The queue producers that post the command words behind cases 0 and 3 are not traced to a UI action.

label: hardware-observed
claim: The discriminating experiment of RESET-ORIGIN-01 ran on the 1.50 body and returned the area-2 branch. limitations: The camera's own indication is the setup menu; no store was read, so the failing check is inferred from the prediction table rather than observed.
Whether the retained header was also invalid is not separated by this run.
One cycle; the experiment was not repeated.

claim: The tick cell 0x400c0800 is ordinary RAM in the log store's region and loader A manages it in three places, mirrored by the 0xd0000 loader. Its initializer 0x40b5c stores zero into the cell and registers the increment function 0x40b24 as callback id 32 through 0x4d8fc in every copy; 0x40b24 calls the selector at [0x4004dae0+0x104] and discards its result, then calls 0x427b8, and only when that returns zero does the callback load the cell, add one and store it, so one core maintains the tick. The block 0x40bb0-0x40c44 runs when the initializer's 0x427b8 check returned zero: it computes [0xFFF91000] with the reciprocal-multiply division by 1875 (magic 0x45E7B273, shift 9), stores the quotient into the cell, forms the remainder with mls against 1875, scales it by 30000 and stores 30000 minus 16 times the remainder into [0xFFF91004], zeroes then writes the control word at [0xFFF91008], and overwrites [0xFFF91004] with 30000, sixteen times 1875, which is the code's own statement of the division and means the phase value does not survive; 0x40c48-0x40c4c then starts 0x41108 with argument 32 on both paths. The loader initializers at 0x4089c/0xd089c publish the cell's address into interface slot +0x174 rather than writing the cell, twelve sites per loader load it (the log writers), image 4 loads it once at 0x00728784, and image 5 conditionally zeroes it at 0x00ec7d80 behind 0x69f8fc with 0x525a. So the tick is the 0xFFF91000 counter divided by 1875, its unit follows that counter's rate rather than a hardware latch, and a debug read of the cell copies bytes without side effects. claim: Host static closure of the X-M1 1.50 body-update write path: staging-to-media mapping, persistence order and marker discipline. The update engine 0x00ec88c8 stages the container main range at 0x42fb7600 (file mode) or 0x42e4025c (in-memory), 0x00db90ac complements every main byte in place, and 0x006ab4cc sources block i at the image base with bit 0 cleared plus i*0x20000, so media offset equals image offset: the 32-byte trailer lands at media 0x24a0000 and its halfword at +0x1e is 0xaaaa, the halfword the first boot record compares at 0x1cec-0x1cfc (the DAT stores it complemented, 0x5555 at DAT 0x24a027a). The writer erases raw block 0x125, the trailer block, first (0x006a9aa4 calls 0x006a9010(0x125,1) and its result is unchecked), optionally pre-erases the contiguous physical run from remap[0] min(10, property 0x276) times, then programs blocks 0..0x125 ascending through the u16 remap table 0x00828580 (cumulative-skip map rebuilt by 0x006a90ac from the bad-block list pointer 0x009552f0 (list at *(0x009552f0)), first filled from the boot record scan of [0, 0x13a)), each block window-check, compare, erase, 64 pages of 0x800 program and verify with mark-bad and same-data retry at budget 0x14-[0x828578], so the completion marker is absent during the write and appears only when the trailer block programs last, its page 0 first. The configuration commit 0x00db91e0 -> 0x0069fea8 -> 0x006a8de0(0x29,33) then rewrites media [0x520000, 0x940000): the DAT auxiliary inputs are preserve lists (98 16-bit and 3 32-bit little-endian offset/length pairs) restoring old ranges over the refreshed 0x42000 template while cache offsets [0x42000, 0x420000) are written back as the RAM cache holds them (the boot load covers only [0, 0x76800) and [0x400000, 0x40fcc0)), and the 0xaa55 cache marker at +0x202 decides whether the next boot accepts the area or falls back to the factory template in raw blocks [7, 10). An interruption before the trailer block page 0 leaves no marker and the first boot record halts at 0x1de8 via the 0x1cc0 compare; an interruption in the configuration commit before device index 0x29 lands loses user settings to the template fallback.

claim: The reviewed probe-straps session 20261008T061646Z-probe-straps ran on XM1-body-01 in a maintenance (jig) boot of official 1.50 and captured 584 bytes over 7 read requests across 5 targets: every captured file matches its journal SHA-256 with 0 mismatches, there is no refusal, uncertainty or error record, both gate readbacks hold (adjustment index 0xf7 = 1 after the enable write and 0 after the restore, the two readback files byte-identical to the 20261008T050828Z session's), and outgoing.v1 equals the 35 write-direction frames of `rehearse probe-straps` in kind, order and bytes with only the session id differing (0x09c6 on the wire, 0x1234 in the rehearsal). The strap registers read 0xfff89014 = 0x00000d4e (bits 11:10 = 3) and 0xfff98000 = 0x00000019 (bits 2:0 = 1); the ROM combines bits 11:10 into bits 4:3 and bits 2:0 into bits 2:0 at 0x8000027c-0x80000284 and its chain maps the value 0x19 to mode 4, so a cold boot with these strap values enters the mode 3-6 handler 0x80000938 with r0 = 1, the 0xfff52000/0xfff52800 controller path that searches pages for the marker words 0x00ffaa55, 0x01234567 and 0x89abcdef, not the mode-1 ffsys.bin/ffboot.bin SD path and not the GPIO-only mode 0. That is consistent with how the body boots: the session is a working maintenance boot of the installed 1.50 application, so its first stage came from this handler's page scan and 0x40000000 staging (inferred, since mode 0 stages nothing and mode 1 serves the documented factory SD-BOOT files). The 0x400a0000 port mirror is byte-identical to the first 64 bytes of the 20261008T045338Z high-known dump: word 0 = 0x00000d62 (bits 11:10 also 3), the other fifteen words are the port-1..15 registers, and it differs from the live 0xfff89014 read in bits 5, 3 and 2 only. The alias windows 0x80010000 and 0x80100000 are both byte-identical to the ROM's first 256 bytes (SHA-256 ce27e3d02a39e1ed362923b40ddbba32e6b20d71a8cd509828901ba95e2192b3), so the same 16 KiB block is served 64 KiB and 1 MiB above the base and a bounded repeated image is refuted. The 0x800002f0 write-back stores the combined word and clears bits 31:5 of 0xfff98000, and a fresh scan of images 4 and 5 finds no access to that address: the only literal 0xfff98000 in either image is the image-4 data word at 0x829158, the nearest block accesses are image-4 stores at 0xfff98504 and image-5 reads at 0xfff98200, so the captured 0x19 is the ROM's recorded boot word rather than raw reset pins or a firmware-written value within the scanner coverage.

claim: Two owner-run jig captures on XM1-body-01 with official 1.50, each taken in the second jig boot of a cycle that differs only in how the maintenance session ended, settle which retained-header bytes the endings write. Cycle A ended with the physical POWER switch (session 20261008T060315Z-dump-ram-high-known); cycle B ended by cutting the dummy-battery supply (session 20261008T060607Z-dump-ram-high-known). Host comparison of the two high-known.bin files: 786 differing bytes, 748 in 0x400a0000-0x400c07ff, 38 in 0x409c2800-0x409c2fff and 0 in the adjustment-cache window 0x41acd800-0x41acdbff, so the cache is byte-identical across the cycles. The companion header at 0x400a00d0, which is the store's 16 bytes as read by the boot record at that boot, reads 0f 0c c3 03 d0 07 00 ff 00 80 00 04 00 00 aa 1b in A and 0f 0c c3 03 d0 07 01 ff 00 80 01 07 00 00 aa 16 in B: both carry the 0xaa marker at byte 14 with byte 15 = -sum(bytes 0..14) (A 0xe5 -> 0x1b, B 0xea -> 0x16), so both are valid headers, and they differ at byte 6 (0x00 versus 0x01), byte 10 (0x00 versus 0x01) and byte 11 (0x04 versus 0x07). The live header at 0x409c281c and the header snapshot at 0x409c29b8 are identical to each other inside each file and carry byte 6 = 0x01 in both, the value the maintenance boot's own sync sets through 0x00643a08(1) at 0x63763c. Both area-2 snapshots are marked records (sequence 0x23c0 in A and 0x23c1 in B at 0x409c2d54) and neither is the ff ff failure image, live/pending/snapshot payloads agree at all five differing offsets, and 0x400a00cc reads 1 in both, so neither captured boot took the defaults path. The remaining 737 differing bytes are the head of the syslog store at 0x400a081e-0x400a1061 plus 11 bytes of boot-local counters and tick words in the companion region, so the only persistent settings difference between the cycles is the retained header. Host reader and writer map over the pinned images: the only writer of header byte 6 bit 0 is property 0x282, whose case body 0x6300e0 edits settings-image byte 6 at 0x630124/0x630128, mirrors it to 0x0089ec06 and pushes all 16 bytes at 0x63012c; its only entry is 0x00643a08, called with 1 from the sync site 0x63763c and with 0 from image-5 0x00ca41e4, the branch that runs only when 0xc021f4 returned -1. Byte 11 bits 0-3 are written by the case bodies of ids 2, 1, 3 and 175 at 0x62fee4, 0x62ff60, 0x62ffe0 and 0x630060, and no case body writes byte 10 at all. Two readers act on the three bytes: the boot action 0x0073cbfc reads byte 6 through 0x6a6e68 at 0x73cc74 and tests bit 0 at 0x73cc78, and the boot record's 0x0001386c tests the low nibble of byte 11 at 0x1388c-0x13898, with its result passed to 0x13b80. The byte-10 accessors are live, not unreferenced: setter 0x6a7de0 is called at image-5 0xf3af7c and 0xf3af88 and getter 0x6a7e68 at image-5 0xf3be00, both mirroring a two-state field of the block at 0x016c0714 (state 3 clears, state 4 sets), so the earlier zero-caller statement holds only for the direct movw/movt forms scanned here. The conclusion recorded with this entry, revised 2026-10-08 by host adjudication (findings section 9), is that neither byte gates the reset. The switch-ending store header at 0x400a00d0 equals the defaults template 0x007cb7f4 for bytes 4 to 14, with bytes 0 to 3 kept and byte 15 recomputed, which is the output shape of 0x006a6fd8 (template memcpy at 0x6a70f0-0x6a70fc), so the ending had already written the defaults image before the captured boot read it. Application-side, 0x0073cbfc reads byte 6 bit 0 at 0x73cc74/0x73cc78 and acts only on the set state, by calling 0x726c74(1,0xf0) at 0x73cc90 and posting the image-5 debug event 0xd3bc34(5) at 0x73cc94-0x73cca8, and a completed maintenance boot writes that bit itself through 0x643a08(1) at 0x63763c, so the clear state marks the orderly terminal branch. Boot-record-side, 0x0001386c (0x1388c-0x13898) verifies byte 11 low nibble 7, its only caller 0x00011d58 folds the result into 0x400a0144 at 0x11f00-0x11f18 through 0x13b80, and 0x13b80 ignores that argument and returns 0 on every path (r0 overwritten at 0x13b98, the 1024-length branch bhs 0x13be8, mov r0, #0 at 0x13c10), so 0x400a0144 is 0 in every boot and the test has no effect. Byte 10 bit 0 differs too (0 after the switch, 1 after the cut), and its writer is the template copy rather than a property: no case body writes image byte 10, so the stored 0x00 can only come from a wholesale 16-byte write, the same write that leaves byte 6 = 0x00 and byte 11 = 0x04 in that store. The byte-10 setter 0x6a7de0 and getter 0x6a7e68 do have callers, at image-5 0xf3af7c/0xf3af88 and 0xf3be00. Because byte 6 bit 0 and byte 11 low nibble read 1 and 7 together after the cut and 0 and 4 together after the switch, the capture pair alone cannot separate them, and the separating arm is the one in findings section 9.6: a no-command jig session ended with the POWER switch, then a second jig session read and ended by cutting the supply, which leaves byte 6 = 1 with bytes 10 and 11 at the template values. 0x400a0140 and 0x400a0144 read 0 in all three captured maintenance boots, matching the 0 that 0x13b80 returns on every path.

claim: The mode-4 boot path of this body's ROM is decoded from the captured 16 KiB block and cross-bound to the 1.50 update container. The mode 3-6 handler 0x80000938 (entered with r0 = 1 for mode 4, device select 1) drives the 0xfff52000/0xfff52800 controller through init 0x80000b74, a six-unit page select 0x80000c2c that accepts a page only while each unit's +0x404 bits 8-15 read 0xff, a 512-byte block read 0x80000d08 with a +0xc8 bits-29:28 status test that fails on 01, and a paged loader 0x80000dec that stages the count field as page groups to 0x40000000 by DMA (128 KiB per group for arg 1; companion block +0x84 = 0x00010001, +0xa0 = 0x00401000, +0xa4 destination, +0xa8 count shifted 17/19/21 for args 1/2/3), advancing past the first two successful page selects, skipping pages whose select fails, retrying a failed unit within the config's budget and writing 0x00030003 to +0xe8 on any failure. The same register map serves the boot record's media reads (record 1 at 0x2b78-0x2ba4 and 0x2c74/0x2f48, 512-byte blocks through 0xfff52400) and image 4's flash driver (0x006ddc90 onward: accessors for +0x00/+0x10/+0x14/+0x50/+0x58/+0x60/+0x78/+0x98/+0xe8, command builder 0x006dde18, address setter 0x006dde74 with a 528-byte (512+16) unit stride for device 1, blank test 0x006ef2f4, page-header and logical-page decode 0x006eecf4), so 0xfff52000 is the internal firmware-media controller, the media whose geometry the update writer programs (128 KiB blocks, 0x800 pages, bad-block remap, trailer block 0x125); the media technology is not named by the bytes, and the flash-like reading (per-512-byte spare bytes, in-page page numbers, bad-block remap) is static-inference. The mode-4 handler scans pages for the 12-byte marker 55 aa ff 00 67 45 23 01 ef cd ab 89 at the start of an even 512-byte unit, applies the found unit through 0x80000304, the register-configuration consumer mode 1 also uses for ffsys.bin, takes its load parameters (bits 10:8 and bit 1 of +0x10, count = +0x18 & 0x3ffff) and hands off through the dispatch to the stub 0x80002298: write 2 to 0xfff98008 and jump to 0x00000000. With the container's config block (media 0 = complemented payload offset 0x48: marker, +0x10 = 0x00000300, +0x18 = 2, verified on the file) the load covers media [0x40000, 0x80000), staging the first boot record (payload record 0x40048, base 0, reset 0x1800) at RAM 0, which is where the live 0x00000000 window holds its vector table, and the second record (payload 0x50048, base 0x10000, vector literal 0x11800) at RAM 0x10000; the ROM validates only the marker, the per-unit statuses and 0x80000304's apply result, and the record's trailer halfword at media 0x24a0000 and its segment table at media 0x140000 are the next gates mapped in reports/update-validation-and-boot.md. The 0x400a0000 port mirror: three loops write the same 64 bytes from the same 16 registers (0xfff89014, stride 0x40) and cannot be told apart by content (boot record 1 at 0x2688, boot record 2 at its offset 0x22c4 = address 0x122c4, image 5 at 0xec7db8); ordering narrows it to the record stage, because the records write at reset under the p14 c2,c0,0 discriminator (0x1828 in both records, calls 0x25d4 and 0x2204), image 5's loop is called only from 0xec797c, whose single call site 0xec8298 sits under 0xec8214, entered when the 0x15c173c aggregate reaches 0x1ff through the step handlers in the 0xec5170 chain, and the captured value (word 0 = 0x00000d62, bit 5 set, bit 2 clear) fits the record-stage sample while the loop's pin-gated path requires 0xfff89014 bit 2 set (its 0xec7898 property exit has no pin gate), which the session read has (0x00000d4e) and the mirror lacks; image 4's classifier 0x6a5aac requires mirror bit 5 set at 0x6a5bd0 and 0x89f818 reads 2 in the captured boots, which requires a record loop to have run. limitations: Host-side static work over the captured block and supplied artifacts; no boot was instrumented, no camera operation ran and nothing was written.

The media technology name is not carried by the bytes; the flash-like reading rests on the 528-byte unit stride, the all-0xff first-16-bytes blank test, the in-page page-number decode and the bad-block remap, all static-inference, and a managed/block-device reading with per-sector tags is not excluded by the register bytes alone.

The +0x404 accept condition's field name and owner are not established; the reading that it is a per-unit tag or status whose 0xff value accepts a unit is static-inference, and the alternative that the checked bits are read data is not excluded.

The 2/4/8 KiB unit sizes and the 128 KiB to 2 MiB page groups are inferences composing the page stride, the page-format selects and the count shifts; the mode-3 (arg 0) addressing is only sketched and is unused on this body.

The staging cross-check assumes the loader advances a contiguous destination across page-select successes and the payload mapping media = payload minus 0x48; the live 0x00000000 window, the trailer at media 0x24a0000 and the second record's vector literal support both, but no live read verifies media content at 0x40000.

A page whose select fails is skipped without failing the load (0x80000ea4 -> 0x80001054), the destination advances only across real unit transfers and the count tracks staged groups, so an unselectable page inside the staged range shifts every later page down one group (128 KiB for arg 1) and the load still returns 0; nothing in the ROM checksums the staged copy and the trailer and segment gates read the media, so neither catches a compacted stage, and a successful load certifies transfer status only and never range integrity. For any future write the six-sub-unit accept tags and the bad-block marks are load-bearing: readers skip unselectable pages, so a write that damages them relocates the image in RAM instead of failing visibly.

The port-mirror attribution rests on order of execution and on the value's bit pattern; an image-5 execution before some capture is not excluded by the dumps, and the bytes do not resolve which core reads 0x4003 from p14, so the record-1 against record-2 twin is unresolved (both write identical bytes).
The R1 judgement is an evidence-level assessment, not a gate acceptance, and it demonstrates no execution, no storage repair and no write route independent of the application.

claim: Host static analysis over the pinned official 1.50 decoded images settles a read-only raw-media read reachable over the existing USB service session. The trigger is one length-1 config function 3 write of 0x35 to adjustment cache index 0x80: FUN_00dc7564 writes the cache byte, then scans the 144-record whitelist at 0x00dc7a84 only when a request starts at index 0x80, and the scan runs on a zero-length request and on a repeat of the same value, so writing the inert flag-0 value 0x33 first is a precondition rather than margin. Record 35 posts queue-7 message 0x1707 with payload 0x35 through FUN_00ed1300; FUN_00eca4c0 maps the payload to group-2 row 34, and the width-7 matrix at 0x00ece2b8 selects action 37 in states 0, 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6 and the inert action 3 in state 4. Action 37 (FUN_00ecc72c -> FUN_00dbcf80 -> FUN_006fba08 -> FUN_006fed00) builds its request from cache byte 0x81 (the spare gate, forced to 0), 0x82 (the block selector, bounded by block + count <= 0x400) and 0x83 (the result code), with a fixed count of 8 device blocks; geometry record 3 at 0x82988c gives 0x20000-byte blocks (page 0x800, PPB 0x40), so one request moves 0x100000 bytes, 0x108000 with the spare gate set, into the staging window 0x4b2ece00. The action opens the storage driver at 0xdbcfe0 and closes it at 0xdbd030 itself, and 0x4b2ece00 is the head of an eight-entry 0x1827c00-byte frame-buffer pool rather than private scratch. Seven whitelist values reach storage-write-capable or state-destroying handlers and the seven are distinct: 0x06, 0x20, 0x21, 0x22, 0x24, 0x28 and 0xc3; six of the seven take the inert action 3 only in state 4 and 0xc3 also in state 6, and state 4 is also the state that defeats the read, so the state word at 0x015c20b0 is a precondition and not a safety gate, and cache byte 0x81 is overloaded four ways and must stay 0. Read-only is established by control-flow reachability over the pinned images rather than by execution: an instruction-level flood fill following BL, intra-function branches and ldr pc jump tables reaches 119 functions from FUN_00dbcf80 and 75 from FUN_006fba08, and neither closure contains FUN_006f0f6c or any erase, commit or settings writer. The lineage carries load-bearing corrections: the first account used geometry record 0 and was wrong by a factor of 8 (0x4000-byte blocks and a 0x20000-byte request against the settled 0x20000-byte blocks and 0x100000-byte request), and it named one destructive value (0x28) where the settled set is seven. This lifts the read-only-primitive half of the Queue C blockage recorded in E-AREA2-PROBE-150 and area2-invalidation.md section 9.1; the capture ran on 2026-10-09 (hardware-observed, E-AREA2-BANKS-150), whose results are recorded there rather than claimed by this static pass.

limitations: Read-only is control-flow reachability over the pinned images, not execution: this claim rests on the reachability closure, the 2026-10-09 run's own observations are recorded in E-AREA2-BANKS-150, and the remaining indirect edges are RTOS primitives in 0x72xxxx dispatching through RAM vtables that static reading cannot resolve.

The hazard set is seven values with the blast radius of each: 0x06 writes one byte into the retained settings image and reaches the device-write primitive FUN_006f0f6c; 0x20 reaches FUN_006f0f6c through its closure; 0x21 runs FUN_0069fe20 and discards unsaved adjustment state by reloading from storage; 0x22 runs FUN_0069fea8 and commits the whole 4 MiB adjustment area from the RAM mirror; 0x24 is FUN_00dbc924, a RAM read/write that can overwrite any accepted address including the staging window; 0x28 is the erase dispatcher FUN_00dbcaa4 whose cases 2 and 3 erase both area-2 banks; 0xc3 reaches FUN_006f0f6c through its closure. The protection is that a closed command never emits these values at index 0x80.

The state word at 0x015c20b0 is a precondition, not a gate: state 4 disables the read as well as every destructive row, and state 6 disarms 0xc3 alone while the read still runs, so no state both reads and disarms the hazard set.

The action leaves the storage driver shut down: the close at 0xdbd030 clears the ready flag with no refcount and no already-open guard, so nothing else may hold storage during the session and the body needs a power cycle before normal use.

The staging window 0x4b2ece00 is shared with imaging, sitting at the head of the frame-buffer pool, so a capture, live view or playback in flight writes the same bytes; which pool layout is live and whether 0x100000 bytes are backed and idle are runtime facts.

Which numbering the service reader wants is settled in docs/evidence.jsonl#E-RAW-MEDIA-NUMBERING-150: the map object is the authority, each bank raw block is its mapped entry plus 0x380, one action-37 request per bank captures it at its own derived selector and offset, a 0xffff entry is refused naming the index, and the placements are runtime map state rather than fixed facts.

Facts a run must read from the camera first: the state halfword at 0x015c20b0, the session-start values of cache 0x80..0x8a, the area-2 map entries, staging-window backing and idle status, any other queue-7 poster during the session, and any other holder of the storage driver.

H1 holds: the store the step-6 ordinary boot read already carried the defaulted settings and that boot wrote nothing the store kept. The step-4 capture holds the user state (payload markers a9 49 49 34 equal in the live, pending and record copies over 0x118 bytes, the C record sequence 0x0a carrying the step-1 ASTIA save at payload +0x24, the frame name C:\DCIM\963_FUJI\DSCF3091.JPG at 0x409c2904); the step-5 capture holds the defaults everywhere (markers 89 09 29 34 in all three copies, frame name erased, area-2 sequence 23c6 with the defaulted 0x118-byte body, C record sequence 0x0b) and its companion at 0x400a00d0 is the defaults template image 0x007cb7f4 for bytes 4..14 with the counters kept and byte 15 recomputed, byte for byte the image cycles A and C carry; the step-7 capture equals step 5 on every decider cell (sequence still 23c6, C record byte-identical over all 52 bytes, 0x409c2944 unchanged). Every capture's own witnesses hold (companion and initializer read 0x409c29b8 both carry 0xaa at byte 14 with byte 15 = -sum(bytes 0..14), marked sequences 23c3/23c5/23c6/23c6 with empty triples and the file-number pair at record +0x24, no ff ff failure template), and the round's own control shows the reads append nothing (the identical step-5 session ended by cut and the step-7 read fill is still 23c6), so the write lies in the step-4 ending's interval and the switch ending committed three store objects: the retained header, an area-2 record carrying the defaulted body, and a custom-record write. The ending's custom record is the reconstruction: the 40-byte payload at 0x0089f838+4 equals the custom defaults table 0x007cb804 plus the cache overlays byte for byte, with 0x0089f85a reading af where the table reads 8f because cache index 0x219 reads 01 and its overlay writes 1 into payload +0x1e bits 5-6; that one-byte difference persists in both the step-5 and step-7 record and is the overlay byte. The four payload bytes the ending reset are +0x0a 49 to 69 (the C record's own shooting mode, bits 5-7 2 to 3), +0x1e cf to af (property 0xf9 bits 5-6, 2 to 1), +0x24 31 to 30 (FILM SIMULATION ASTIA code 1 back to PROVIA code 0) and +0x25 46 to 07, with the parity regions moving with the body and the settings image's custom payload at 0x409c295c moving at the same four offsets. Companion byte 6 moved 00 to 01 across a boot that stopped at the START MENU language selection and was answered by nothing, bounding the completion mark to the boot's own sync interval with no user answer, no completed setup flow and no shooting screen required, and showing the ordinary-mode POWER/OFF did not run the template write (byte 6 would read 00 at step 7). The control arm (steps 2 and 3) is a fourth settings-preserving cut-ending instance and the second with commands sent in the session: the two earlier trials of E-JIG-POWERCUT-PRESERVES-150 were no-command, E-ADJ-READ-150 records the third (its read-config entry at 17:53 with 1342 requests and the owner's preserved-settings report), and this one ran the reviewed read-only dump pair and its gate enable/restore cycle before the cut. label: static-inference
claim: X-M1 1.50 has no color-space property or setting at all (the first of the three cases this pass was to decide; static-inference over byte-read bytes of the pinned images, with the owner's negative search in E-COLOR-SPACE-OWNER-150): no property id, no values array, no menu node, no label entry and no stored field is bound to color space. What exists is label text and a metadata field. Label text: COLOR SPACE, sRGB and Adobe RGB are UTF-16 strings in the English language slot and the German and Japanese dumps carry the translated trio (string ids 0x647/0x648/0x649), and the plain image carries ASCII copies at 0x011206cc-0x011206e8. Nothing uses them: the id4 node map names no node with any of the three labels, an aligned halfword and word scan of the whole 2,631,680-byte id4 image for 0x647/0x648/0x649 finds no label entry, no values array and no node header (only code, tone-curve data and a run of adjustment-cache index pairs at 0x007ce224 in the shape the FUN_006cc604-family readers index), the 289 conversion tables reachable through the pointer array at 0x0081b09c carry no color-space rows, and the 57-field C-payload map carries no color-space field. Metadata: the plain image's image-parameter info screen decodes the record word at +0x184 as 0 sRGB, 1 AdobeRGB, other blank (FUN_01118a00; ldr r3,[r3,#0x184] at 0x011930c), the EXIF summary's color-space halfword at +0x4ca is initialised to the constant 1 (sRGB) by FUN_011c2ecc and overwritten only by a parsed file's tag 0xa001 (FUN_011c36f8), FUN_012770a0 tests it equal to 1 for a print flag, and the id5 makernote builders write no color-space field. The camera's own frames record EXIF ColorSpace sRGB (tag 0xa001 = 1) with InteroperabilityIndex R98 and no color-space tag in the FujiFilm makernote (hardware-observed frames read host-side). The recorded value is therefore fixed sRGB, not derived from any setting: the metadata field's capture-time producer is unproved, and one 1.50-era frame would close that link end to end.
scope: The pinned official 1.50 images (id4 at 0x0061c400, id5 at 0x00bf1a00, plain at 0x01100000, the English language slot), the id4 node map and C-payload map of this tree, and the S01/S02 frames shot on XM1-body-01 under firmware 1.00; claims are 1.50 except where the frame evidence names 1.00
limitations: The frame evidence is from firmware 1.00 (the S01/S02 frames); no 1.50-era frame is in this tree, so the 1.50 recorded value rests on the static map plus the constant sRGB default in the EXIF summary.
The capture-time producer of the metadata color-space field and of the emitted tag 0xa001 is unproved: the mapped corpus writes +0x4ca only from the constant default and the parser.

About forty C-payload fields keep no bound meaning, so the negative cannot exclude a color-space role for one of them by name; none of them is identified as color space by any label, node, values array or consumer.

claim: Byte-read resolution of which numbering the raw-media read wants for the area-2 banks, from the pinned official 1.50 decoded image 4 (static-inference). The descriptor-layer area read resolves its map-relative index with FUN_006fca60, which reads the u16 at map + 0x10 + 2 * index, returns minus one for a 0xffff entry and otherwise adds the map object start word (file offsets 0xe0668 to 0xe0690: ldr r2,[r1]; ldr r3,[r1,#8]; add r0,r1,r0,lsl #1; ldrh r0,[r0,#16]; movw r3,#0xffff; cmp r0,r3; addne r0,r0,r2; mvneq r0,#0), and the read then feeds that resolved block to FUN_006f1a74 as block * PPB + page (mla at 0xe0798, bl at 0xe07a8). The action 37 raw-media read FUN_006fed00 feeds the same entry point block * PPB with no map resolution (mov r0,r5 at 0xe2978, bl at 0xe2988). The two namings therefore converge on one entry point, so the reader takes physical block numbers used directly and the blocks holding the banks are the map-resolved entry + 0x380, not the encoded descriptor bases 0x3d6 and 0x3d7, which equal those only under the identity map. The map is runtime state that the FUN_006fea48 scan rebuilds at install, so a placement is read per run and never assumed: the 2026-10-08 capture (E-DUMP-RAM-150) showed map start 0x380 and entries 0x2c and 0x32 at map + 0xBC and map + 0xBE, which put the banks at 0x3ac and 0x3b2 in different 8-block windows, while the same object at map + 0xB0 holds entries 0x50 and 0x51, both 0xffff. The read-media operation therefore issues one action-37 request per bank at its own derived selector and offset, refuses a 0xffff entry naming the index before the block arithmetic, and captures each bank 0x20000-byte block.
scope: X-M1 official 1.50 area-2 raw-media read numbering and the read-media derivation built on it. Host-only: no camera enumerated, opened, written or commanded. The captured map values are cited from the recorded dump and are one body at one moment.
commands: sha256sum over the artifacts listed above
limitations: The chain is static reading of pinned bytes: this pass touched no camera, and the run that later exercised the chain is the 2026-10-09 read-media session (hardware-observed, E-AREA2-BANKS-150), recorded separately.

The map is runtime state rebuilt at install by the FUN_006fea48 scan, so the captured entries 0x2c and 0x32 and the resulting blocks 0x3ac and 0x3b2 are one body at one moment and are not fixed facts about the banks.

Whether FUN_006f1a74 applies the u16 remap table at 0x828580 internally is untraced here; both namings converge at that entry point so they are treated identically, and the captured table is the identity.
The map start word added by FUN_006fca60 is the map object first word, 0x380 in the capture and firmware-fixed; a body showing a different start would need it read live.

The mode byte's one use in both engine-driver copies is bit 24 of the engine length register set when the byte is not 4 (boot kick 0x3c54 writes 0xfff43044; the relocated copy compares byte +0x10 with 4 at 0x684414-0x684430 before the same write); segment-table words 7/8 have no consumer in the boot's id-4 path 0x2250 (words 1, 3, 4, 5, 6 only), the id-0/1 path 0x1d08/0x231c (1, 4, 5), image 4's id-5 loader 0x6a96c0 (1, 3, 4, 5, 6; its decompress branch is the 0x657184 struct read) or the id-6 loader 0x6a9844 (5, 6), so ids 4 and 5 are hard-wired to the hardware engine and a stored image would reach it as a token stream; uncompressed images would not fit their flash windows (0x282800 against 0x160000, 0x4f1e60 against 0x2e0000). //lz:lz-codec (FujiAF.Lz.Encode over FujiAF.Lz.Format) emits greedy longest matches with the length capped at the distance and 15, minimum 3, nearest distance on ties, literal runs to 127, and the stock feed-page fill (runs clamp at page ends and absorb one byte rather than strand it; matches with four and three bytes of page left become literal prefixes plus the tail match at the same distance); re-encoding lz/id4-0061c400.bin and lz/id5-00bf1a00.bin reproduces the 0x146567-byte and 0x2c66d1-byte stock records at payload 0x160048 and 0x2c0048, both the stock and the re-encoded records decode back to the pinned images under the existing strict decoder fflzd (copied unchanged to lz/fflzd.c), a 189-case synthetic corpus and a 513-case swept page-geometry family round-trip through it with the header arithmetic, page-aligned tokens and stock token domains checked, and a 1,001-length feed-aligned sweep shows the refusals live. Three guards close defect classes without touching the matcher or the stock fill shapes: a literal run at the 127 cap with 129 bytes of page left flushes one byte short (a full-cap flush there strands one byte of page and the old code answered with a zero-length run), a zero-length run flush is a hard error, and the encoder refuses a total_len on a feed boundary (FeedAlignedTotalLen) or a record over its flash window (WindowExceeded) and re-walks its tokens (InvalidTokenization); the pinned reproduction still passes on both images with the guards applied.
scope: Pinned public X-M1 1.50 payload (payload-complement.bin) and the two decoded images, host-only runs 2026-10-09; stock token statistics are 317,995 and 623,410 matches with 0 of them longer than their distance and minimum distance 3; the stock records use 92 and 96 percent of their flash windows.
limitations: The engine's interpretation of mode values other than 4 is hardware: the driver reduces the byte to bit 24 of the length register and nothing more is observable from the code.

The grammar's unused corners (control 0x00, distance 0, length 0, overlapping copies, distances 1-2) are refused by fflzd, never occur in the stock streams and are never emitted here; engine behaviour on them is unproved.

Token behaviour across a feed kick and interior pages that do not fill to their end is untested: the stock streams never exhibit either and the encoder never produces them. The engine's end-of-stream behaviour when the final kick is a full chunk is untested and the encoder refuses that geometry, so the refusal is a guard against an untested shape rather than a test of it.

For a modified input the byte-for-byte reproduction is evidence of model fidelity only: the engine has been observed on two streams, and the patched record is safe to build and review, not safe to trust. No camera has accepted a rebuilt container; the install decision remains open.

claim: Owner-run body test on XM1-body-01 running official 1.50 (hardware-observed): with the mode dial at C, changing a setting and then moving the dial away and back leaves the edit in place; a power off/on with the switch drops the edit unless CUSTOM SET was run. This refutes the derived consequence that C-record edits revert at the next bank reload; the dial transition reloads nothing over the record. The 1.50 code agrees (byte-read, conclusion static-inference): FUN_006309c4's per-write reload FUN_0061d9ec covers only the ordinary block (image 0x10-0x127) and never the slot record at 0x140, the setter's record branch writes bank RAM only (bank 0 slot record at 0x0096cda4 with bank 2 at 0x0089ed40 written in parallel from the literal at 0x0062a144), a class change rebinds the current-record selection without copying (FUN_00636230 writes the class cell 0x00951564, FUN_006439e0 resolves the record per access, FUN_006379d8 writes only a guard cell and FUN_006438ec reloads nothing), and the only routine that reloads the slot record from the image mirror (FUN_00630a34 through FUN_0061d994) runs at boot init (FUN_00639b1c -> FUN_00638d0c -> FUN_0061c8cc) and at the UI/session reset FUN_00d3c20c (FUN_00d3c3b4 case 0xc), never on the dial path. The mirror at 0x140 is written only by the CUSTOM SET copy FUN_00630b14's explicit FUN_0072b3d0 store and the boot record read 0x006a8abc, and only that store commits area 3 through FUN_006a6f3c -> FUN_006a86c4, which is why CUSTOM SET is the only persistence route. The observation also confirms P15 behaviourally: an edit dying at a power off that persists ordinary settings shows the C-position write went to slot 0 rather than the ordinary block, so the mode-class cell selects the record while the dial is at C on this body.
scope: One owner-run behaviour test on XM1-body-01 running official 1.50 (dial at C, edit, dial away and back, power off/on, with and without CUSTOM SET) plus host-only static reading of the pinned 1.50 images for the mechanism; no bytes were read on the body and no RAM window accompanied the test.
limitations: No RAM window accompanied the body test: the class cell value at C is inferred from the outcomes (an edit that dies at a power off which persists ordinary settings cannot have been in the ordinary block), not read directly; a C-position-correlated RAM window still closes P15's last link.

The action is FUN_00c32320 (0x00c32320, image 5): it reads the framework's action parameter cells 0x0094f650 and 0x0094f654 (the block 0x0094f64c-0x0094f65c is written by FUN_0063270c, id4) and calls the reset dispatcher FUN_00d4e4d4, whose first branch handles the value 0x91, the item's id in the values array; the handler word 0x00c32320 sits at pointer 0xd04764 in the image-5 pointer run that also holds the CUSTOM SET action 0x00c74e5c at 0xd04214 (that function's tail calls FUN_00d4e2a0(4,0,0), the copy of the current settings into slot 0). The custom branch clears 0x00954294, stores reset class 3 into 0x00944564 through FUN_00638220, and calls FUN_00d4e2a0(row, row, 1) with both rows from 0x0094f654; that routine returns before any write unless the destination row is 0, writes property 0xe9 for slot 0 from the getter's defaults branch (0x007cb80e >> 5 = 3) and calls FUN_00630b14(row, 0, 1). FUN_00630b14 walks about ninety properties, takes each value from FUN_0061e110(prop, 0, 1, srcSlot), the defaults read through the pointer 0x007cb804 at 0x28*slot + payload offset, writes it into destination slot code 0, and, because that code is not 1, stores the 0x28-byte record from 0x0096cda4 to settings-image offset 0x140 through FUN_0072b3d0 -> FUN_006a6f3c -> FUN_006a86c4, which compares record bytes [2, 0x2c) and appends the record to area 3 through FUN_006ac7d4 on a difference; the dispatcher tail then runs the settings notify 0x00d466c8. Scope: slot row 0, per-slot, with no all-slots loop; the ordinary settings block and slot rows 1 and 2 are untouched; the mirror and area 3 are written on the spot, so the record reads as the per-slot defaults (film simulation PROVIA, image quality FINE, index byte +0x27 zero, mode field 3). Consequence for RC1: selecting CUSTOM RESET clears a stored C recipe, index byte and payload fields included, and commits the default record to area 3, which the design handles as index 0 = no recipe, as a user-invokable route beside the jig-cycle constructor.

label: static-inference
claim: A diagnostic X-M1 1.50 SD-BOOT card is buildable from held material without ZJ02217. Byte-read: ROM mode 1 requests 1024 ffsys.bin bytes into 0xfff00004 for 0x80000304; concatenating payload.bin[0x48,0x248) and [0x848,0xa48) supplies the corrected stock config, preserving its seven pair writes and the 0xfff52050=0x22312131 and 0xfff52078=0x605 driver cross-checks (E-CONFIG-APPLY-150). The config-driven values and branches match the mode-4 apply the body survives at every boot (hardware-observed); equal incoming MMIO state or survival in modes 1/2 is unproved. Byte-read: mode 1 stages ffboot.bin's directory size at 0x40000000 in chunks up to 0x8000 and hands off in A32 to 0x00000000, checking no record header, checksum, model, version, trailer, segment table or destination-size bound. Static-inference: a project-owned bounded little-endian A32 record with an entry at byte 0, RAM signature and halt is host-constructible, not dependent on vendor boot-record bytes; it cannot alone demonstrate observable R2 execution. Mode 1 opens only ffsys.bin and ffboot.bin, mode 2 uses raw blocks and mode 4 uses internal media, so ffuser.bin is not a ROM requirement on these routes (byte-read); its copy instruction is specific to the factory procedure (static-inference), with its vendor-payload role unproved. Byte-read: FAT mount 0x80001ba0 first tests sector 0 for 55 aa at +510 and FA at +54 or +82, accepting a FAT superfloppy; otherwise it reads only the first MBR entry at +0x1be, requires a nonzero type, takes its +8 start LBA and checks that FAT boot sector. The earlier MBR-only description is withdrawn. The stack assumes 512-byte sectors, parses FAT12/16/32 by data-cluster count plus 2 at thresholds 0xff7/0xfff7, uses the first FAT and follows cluster chains, and compares root-directory 11-byte short names FFSYS   BIN and FFBOOT  BIN. Static-inference: a first-primary MBR FAT32 volume with these two files is a conservative host-buildable image; fragmentation is supported, a bootable/active flag is not required, GPT/exFAT and later partitions are not parsed. A working mode-1/2 entry is the single external gate to this diagnostic lane, not unobtained service files; the document-supported press is evidence-negative on this body after the owner's 2026-10-09 observations.
scope: Host-only research and record correction over the pinned captured ROM and official 1.50 complemented payload; no new payload, image builder or card image delivered, no card prepared and no camera or USB device touched. The factory MAIN PWB Initialize package remains unobtained and is distinct from a project diagnostic card.
commands: Read pinned bootrom.dis mode-1 loader 0x8000082c-0x80000934, FAT mount/name/chain/read closure 0x80001678-0x80002090, and SD wait helper 0x80001618-0x80001648; compared with E-CONFIG-APPLY-150 and E-SDBOOT-FILE-COVERAGE-150

The stock config supplies byte-identical config-driven effects, but modes 1/2 enter without the mode-4 internal-media initialization; incoming MMIO state and unbounded config polls remain hardware questions.

The ROM file-read helper can return success after EOF-shortening without the mode-1 caller checking transferred length; the host must enforce the complete 1024-byte config, nonempty bounded executable and sector-rounded DMA destination span.

A useful observable report-sector R2 diagnostic needs a project-owned bounded CMD24 SD write helper, its write-set audit and host tests. The ROM supplies reads only and 0x80001618 polls status without a software iteration limit; these are unfinished host deliverables, not a missing vendor file.
The service payload's ffuser.bin role and behavior on a nonblank board remain unproved; omission is justified only for the decoded ROM routes and project-owned diagnostic.
A camera exercise awaits the owner's go and the required independent review of new write-capable bytes. No alternative SD-entry actuation or board modification is authorized or proposed.
Diagnostic-card buildability supplies no restorative writer and claims no repair capability.

Byte-read: mode 0 hands off to unstaged RAM, modes 3/5/6 select internal-media formats through 0xfff52000, and mode 7 initializes 0xfff56000, reads a 1024-byte config, then requests a counted bulk receive into 0x40000000. Byte-read: ROM staging does not authenticate boot-record bytes; mapped record-1 failures halt or wait and mapped record-2 optional validity failure continues, with no failure-triggered SD or USB rescue path found. label: hardware-observed
claim: Owner-run press exercise on XM1-body-01 running official 1.50 on 2026-10-09, no card and no USB at any step (hardware-observed): power on while pressing the Function button together with each button on the camera except the flash release, and together with the sub-command dial press, booted the application normally in every combination. The one exception, Function plus DISP/BACK, reached the ordinary firmware-upgrade screen, an application surface reached after a normal boot (E-UPDATE-ENTRY-KEY-BIND-150), so it also ran the mode-4 path, and no combination produced a dark or halted body. A normal boot is a mode-4 run: the mode-select inputs 0xfff89014 bits 11:10 and 0xfff98000 bits 2:0 are read at reset before any media is examined (byte-read 0x80000274/0x80000278, called at 0x80000130 before the dispatch), the dispatch runs one handler per boot and halts at 0x80000020 on any nonzero return with no fall-through (byte-read), modes 1 and 2 exhaust their bounded no-card retries and return -1 (byte-read), and the cardless runs of modes 0, 3, 5, 6 and 7 are not fully decoded (static-inference: none of them stages the mode-4 record), so the mode reading rests on identifying the observed normal boots with mode 4 rather than on an absence of dark halts. Every combination tried held the mode-select bits at their mode-4 values. label: independently-reproduced
claim: A verification gate that re-derives the value it must check cannot fail, and one did in the image-replacement chain (host run and byte reads over the pinned 1.50 container; corrected build independently reproduced). The container's record-4 header word 1 is the record length the loader's feed arithmetic reads (total_len = 0x14 + stream length; stock 0x146567 with stream 0x146553), not the stream length the field contract's label said; a short value feeds the decompressor fewer bytes than the stream holds, drops tokens and lands in the engine's hang-shaped failure inside the unrecoverable window. The first chain run wrote the stream length into that word (0x1465cc where 0x1465e0 belonged) and the rebuilt-stream gate passed anyway because it re-assembled the record header from its own derivation instead of reading the container's stored words, so the wrong stored word never reached the decoder. The fix reads the artifact and compares: word 1 is checked against 0x14 + the stream bytes, the emission checks run against the bytes read back from the assembly instead of the derived header, and the fflzd gate consumes the five stored words with the decoder's own arithmetic checking them. The same-shape sweep over the chain: record-header word 0 compares against the attached decoded image, word 2 against the stored word 1's ceil, words 3 and 4 against constants, and the three checksum words against a fresh complement-sum over the assembled bytes; the segment entry's size and bss words and the trailer words that mirror entry 4 are relations between stored words (size = decoded + 0x28, bss = load + decoded, bss end = id-5 load, trailer = entry-4 load/size) with no re-derivation in the check path; the carried set compares against the source container and the pinned stock restore lists. No other derivation-that-masks instance was found in the chain. The lesson for any new gate: verify by reading the artifact and comparing, never by recomputing from the same derivation that produced it, because a recomputation agrees with itself whatever the artifact says.
scope: Host tooling over the pinned public X-M1 1.50 container and one probe rebuild; the claim is about the gate design, not about camera behavior; host-only.
limitations: The defect class is established by construction and by the corrected run; that no other instance exists is a sweep result over this chain's checks, not a property any future gate inherits automatically.

The loader's feed arithmetic (word 1 minus 0x14 bytes fed, no others) is static-inference from the mapped driver copies; the hang-shaped failure is the engine error branch's documented shape, not a hardware-observed hang.
The parse layer the comparisons trust is itself proven only by the byte-exact round trip on stock and the synthetic suite.
A short word 1 in a container that passed review and installed would hang the boot in the invalid-application class with the recorded recovery limits; nothing was installed and no camera was touched.

label: static-inference
claim: The boot card payload's RAM signature is not recoverable, so a post-attempt read cannot detect it (static-inference over byte-read ROM and record bytes plus one hardware-observed low-RAM capture; reports/boot-card-detection.md). The signature sits at RAM 0x00000100 inside the payload's own sector-rounded staged span at 0x40000000, the alias of RAM 0. Every ROM route that reaches the application stages its first block there before the handoff jump: the mode-4 route this body takes sets destination 0x40000000 with count [config+0x18] & 0x3ffff = 2 page groups of 128 KiB (the config word at payload.bin + 0x60 reads 0x00000002), so it writes RAM [0x00000000, 0x00040000) from media [0x40000, 0x80000) before the jump, and the byte staged to RAM 0x00000100 is the first boot record's byte at that offset, sixteen 0xff bytes in the pinned record (decode/boot-40048.bin offset 0x100); mode 1 stages ffboot.bin in chunks up to 0x8000 to 0x40000000 and its DMA dispatcher reads whole sectors for destinations in [0x40000000, 0x80000000) whatever the requested sub-sector count, so that route's first 512 bytes land at RAM 0 too; mode 2 reads raw blocks by DMA to 0x40000000. The reader cannot get there first: the read primitive is opcode 0x200001 function 2 (address at +0x1c), which acts only inside a maintenance session under the running application, and it already read the 256 bytes at 0x00000000 in an ordinary boot (E-BOOTROM-EXTENT-150, window 00000000.bin), so the region is reachable and holds staged record content, not the signature, by the time any read can run; the payload's halt is wfi with IRQ and FIQ masked, and the only exit from a halted body is a battery pull, which removes DRAM power with retention unproved for every address. Bounded by the ROM environment, an observable payload needs a channel the ROM does not provide, because the ROM's SD code is initialization plus reads (command table 0x800022e0-0x8000232f, read command 0x113a at base+0x0e) and its internal-media code is the init 0x80000b74, page select 0x80000c2c, block read 0x80000d08 and paged loader 0x80000dec, all reads whose failure paths write only MMIO. The card's reserved report sector at LBA 34816 is the one target that survives the next boot and power removal and is readable on a host card reader: it needs the project CMD24 helper with the write command words, FIFO direction, CRC policy and completion handling established, bounded waits with distinct failure codes, one write and a read-back. A RAM record instead needs an address whose no-writer argument holds from reset through the read plus retention evidence across the battery pull, and neither exists.
scope: Host-only static trace over the captured 0x4000 boot-ROM artifact, the official 1.50 complemented payload, the pinned first boot record and the existing low-RAM capture; no card written and no camera or USB device touched. The verdict covers RAM 0x00000100, the address the built payload uses, and the general bound on what an observable payload needs; it claims no entry.
limitations: The trace is byte-read and static-inference over ROM, record and payload bytes plus one hardware-observed low-RAM capture; no payload was executed and no post-attempt read was performed.
Whether a later stage or the running application also writes RAM 0x00000100 is unproved; the first staging already overwrites it, so the verdict does not depend on that.

Extending the read primitive to a 0x00000100 window is static-inference from the captured window on the same page; no operation's fixed window list contains it, so a code change and the owner's go would be needed to run it.
Retention of any RAM address across the battery pull that exits a halted body is unproved, so no alternative RAM address is established as observable.
The reporting payload's SD write path remains unproved and unbuilt: this entry names what it needs, not a delivered artifact.

claim: No storage for a preset name exists on the X-M1 1.50 custom-setting record, and the free space is measured rather than assumed (static-inference over the byte-read field map and the inherited record map; host-only, reports/named-recipe-reach.md section 2.1). The record's only other unclaimed space is the two compared bytes at record +0x02/+0x03, which have no writer in image 4, and the settings image's ordinary block tail at image bytes 0x124, 0x125 and 0x127, which are 0x00 in the image-resident defaults block 0x0089e8e0 and unclaimed by any property. Total unclaimed space is about 9 bytes and 5 bits against the tens of bytes a name needs at 2 bytes per UTF-16 unit, so every naming design must supply its own storage. Payload bytes +0x00-+0x03 are unbound, not proven unused: a register-indirect or out-of-image reader is not excluded.

limitations: The unbound payload bytes have no writer or reader bound; their use as name storage would need its own writer and its own commit-path review.

label: static-inference
claim: Host static closure of the 1.50 log store's type-0x0f records as the kernel message trace. The only writer of type 0x0f is loader A's 0x41c8c, whose only caller in the 41,683-function decompilation export is image 4's 0x00726478; the image-4 startup 0x0069d160 installs 0x00726478 as a hook through 0x00724cbc (the one-instruction store _DAT_4089ea94 = param_1), so the trace covers every send the hook sees and not only UI events. The record's word at +4 is {receiver u8, sender u8, message id u16} little-endian and the record's task byte at +1 is the writer's TPIDRURW, so a record names its sender. 0x007262cc initialises the mode byte 0x40a5b5e0 to 0, the filter enable 0x40a5b5e1 to 1, the threshold 0x40a5b5e2 to 1, the write offset 0x40a5b5e4 to 8 and the trace buffer pointer 0x40a5b5ec to 0x41ac9800, and 0x00726478 drops an id whose code from the 1716-entry sorted table at 0x81485c is below the threshold. The AF ids 0x1394, 0x13a5, 0x1a0d, 0x3b0d, 0x3b32, 0x3f0d, 0x3f2e and 0x420c each carry code 1 in that table, so the AF request, search, lens and result messages are inside the trace's allowlist. No AF function in image 5 calls loader A's writers 0x41c8c, 0x41a34 or 0x42188, so the AF orchestration task writes no record of its own; the helper 0x006c633c does call the string writer 0x42188 with the strings IBW_S, IBWAIT and IBW_E, and the capture shows those records under the lensdc task byte 0x32.
scope: X-M1 1.50 pinned images, host-only static analysis
limitations: Three type-0x72 call sites pass computed string pointers (0x00e91d50, 0x00e93c34, 0x00e457c0), so the fixed-string census does not cover every string the store can receive.
The word layout is read from the single writer and its single caller; the kernel side that calls the installed hook is indirect and appears in the export as no call site.
The trace is an allowlist, not a complete send log: an id absent from the table at 0x81485c is dropped, and membership was checked only for the ids named.
The filter enable, threshold and buffer pointer are read from the initialiser, not from a live body, so a later writer could change them.
The absence of AF-side calls to the loader writers is a direct-call scan and cannot exclude a call through a computed pointer.

label: static-inference
claim: The mujin task's delay unit and the host-command latency place the AUTO_ACT arm write inside the gate-test window with two orders of magnitude to spare (static-inference over byte-read of the pinned X-M1 1.50 decoded images; the tick rate, the three cell samples and the 53-session latency set are hardware-observed from this body's own capture journals). Byte-read: the task entry FUN_00ed2ce0 calls FUN_00ed2c90 (bl at 0xed2cec), whose first action is mov r0,#1000 / bl 0x00ed1660 at 0xed2ca8-0xed2cac; FUN_00ed1660 is a one-instruction wrapper (push {r11,lr}; add r11,sp,#4; bl 0x00723ce8; pop {r11,pc} at 0xed1660-0xed166c); the second wait is mov r0,#4000 / bl 0x00ed1660 at 0xed2cbc-0xed2cc0 and the sender's trailing wait is mov r0,#100 at 0xed2c84; the kernel delay 0x00723ce8 loads the interface pointer at 0x0096bd20, calls its +0x1618 selector, and for a nonzero argument calls interface[selector]+0x4c with the delay argument in r0, while a zero argument takes the +0x11c arm instead. Hardware-observed rate: the adjustment-independent tick cell the host samples as tick=400c0800 reads 72436, 72461 and 87394 in the three checkpoints of the body's own read-log session 20261009T064945Z (journal tuples at line 65 and line 17027, 149.72 s apart on the session's monotonic clock); the first and last are monotonic, so the counter advances 14958 units in 149.72 s, 99.9 Hz, a 10 ms unit, with no wrap needed to explain the pair; two short spans in the same session give 0.87 to 1.06 kHz for sub-second intervals, which the 16-bit field at +0x06 of the ring entries explains as the same counter's low halfword. The unit is therefore 10 ms, so 1000 is about 10 s and 4000 about 40 s, and the test instant is about 10 s after task start. Hardware-observed host cost: over all 53 service sessions under private-data/sessions, the interval from the session's first journal line (the operation's prepared record, before device selection) to the first outgoing transfer (the C0 ControlWrite) runs 89.35 ms minimum, 92.95 ms median, 122.56 ms 90th percentile and 182.76 ms maximum, with 47 of 53 sessions between 89 and 104 ms. The comparison is therefore a measured 89-183 ms against a measured 10 s, and the one term without a measurement is boot-to-enumeration, which is where the image-5 init that creates the task also sits in a maintenance boot (the task's creation is the bl at 0x00d98660 inside FUN_00d985a4, and the boot-log captures carry the image-5 load on maintenance boots as on ordinary ones, LOAD-TIMING-01). The arm write is bounded to RAM 0x41acd8a2, is cleared by any power cycle through the boot load 0x0069f204, and is never persisted, because the queue-7 commit post 0x1707 exists only for a start index of 0x80.
scope: Pinned public X-M1 1.50 DAT and its decoded images 4 and 5, plus this body's own capture journals (read-log 20261009T064945Z and all 53 sessions under private-data/sessions); host-only, no camera was enumerated, opened or commanded.
limitations: The 10 ms unit is bound by comparing the cell to the host's monotonic clock; the short-span samples in the same session disagree with the long span by up to 10x, and the 16-bit-low-halfword explanation for that is static-inference, not observation.

Boot-to-enumeration is not measured: no capture records the interval from power-on to USB readiness, so the window's lower bound rests on the measured host cost plus the fact that the task is created during the application's own image-5 init.
The tick cell's writer is not bound to a named kernel timer in these images; the rate is measured, not derived from a scheduler configuration.
The latency set is this body's 53 sessions on this host; a different host or a cold libusb cache could shift it, and the four sessions above 120 ms are unexplained.

label: static-inference
claim: The AUTO_ACT firing experiment is no longer blocked for the RAM-only form, and it is now a bounded watch rather than a race; what stays blocked is the persistent form, on the same boundedness property (static-inference over byte-read, superseding the timing paragraph of reports/auto-act-arming.md section 2 and the blocked verdict of E-AUTOACT-ARM-150). Superseded claim: the earlier verdict held that a byte written by the host in a session could not be relied on to make that session's camera read the card because the test runs a few seconds after boot and a hand-started bazel run cannot be counted into that window. Measured now: the test runs at task start plus 1000 delay units, the delay unit measures 10 ms on this body's own clock samples (E-AUTOACT-TIMING-150), and the host's first byte costs 89-183 ms across all 53 captured sessions, so the write is two orders of magnitude inside the window. The persistent form's block is unchanged: reaching storage with index 0xa2 still requires the whole-area commit 0x0069fea8 of 0x420000 bytes from the RAM mirror, triggered by a config write of 0x22 to index 0x80, which the End Setting live protocol forbids in any value. Corrections carried into the report: the parser input-length word is 0x16777ac and the selector is 0x16777c0 (both in dump-ram segment id5-bss-2), not 0x16677ac/0x16677c0; the loader's clear is 0x10764 bytes at 0x166704c, not 0x1764, and the statement capacity that follows is about 300 at the 0xe0-byte stride rather than 26; and the disarm is load-bearing rather than free, because both senders 0x00ed2b8c and 0x00ed2be4 re-read the gate byte when they run and FUN_00ed2c34 re-tests it before them, so a disarm between the test and the sends suppresses the run silently. label: static-inference
claim: The AUTO_ACT script executor needs no DCAA counterpart and the first runnable script is 13 bytes (static-inference over byte-read of the pinned 1.50 decoded images; reports/auto-act-script.md sections 5, 11 and 12). Self-queue model: the three sends on the path (0x3300, 0x3302, 0x3305) are all addressed to task/op id 35, the id the mujin task is created under, and the task's loop receives from 35 through id4 0x725318, so the loader's own 0x3305 (0xed1670) returns to the same task and every statement handler queues the next 0x3305; 0x3301 and 0x3303 are constructed nowhere in the pinned images and their callback slot 0x16777c8 is only cleared (0xed16d8) and read (0xed14f0), never set, so a loaded script runs to END unattended and a no-match code stops at the {0x1a,0} terminator, posts nothing, and the task blocks in the receive. label: static-inference
claim: On X-M1 1.50 the ROM has no application-validity fallback and nothing in the decoded software sets the SD-boot selector (static-inference over byte-read ROM, record and image bytes; reports/sd-boot-claim-test.md). The mode detect 0x80000260 reads 0xfff89014 bits 11:10 at 0x80000274 and 0xfff98000 bits 2:0 at 0x80000278 once per reset and derives the mode at 0x8000027c-0x80000300, writing the combined word back at 0x800002f0 with bits 2:0 preserved; the pre-detect path from 0x80000028 touches only MMIO 0xfff89008 and 0xfff88084 and SRAM, so the selection precedes every media, card, key and application access. SD modes: mode 1 (SD/FAT channel 0, dispatch 0x8000014c) needs the high pair zero; mode 2 (raw channel 1, dispatch 0x80000164) needs the low selector 4 with a nonzero high pair; this body presents 3 and 1 and boots mode 4 (E-STRAP-READ-150). The dispatch calls one handler per boot and halts at 0x80000020 on any nonzero return (0x800001f8-0x800001fc), and the call sites of 0x8000082c, 0x8000071c and 0x80000938 are the dispatch entries only. The ROM validates no staged record: mode 1 stages the directory-declared ffboot.bin to 0x40000000 and hands off to RAM 0 with no header, checksum, version or size check, and the mode 3-6 handler stages page groups after the marker scan with no checksum. Every handler failure returns -1 after clearing 0xfff88084 bit 0 (mode 1 0x80000858-0x80000860, mode 2 0x80000750-0x80000758, mode 3-6 0x80000978-0x80000984 and 0x80000a58-0x80000a60), so a damaged internal-media application produces a dark halt and not an SD boot. The record side matches: record 1's trailer gate 0x1cc0 and its storage, segment and decompressor failures call the teardown 0x1de8 and self-loop (0x1f18, 0x1f58, 0x1f90, 0x1fd8, 0x226c, 0x3d28), with no branch to the SD handlers, the ROM or a reset, and record 2 continues past its companion check instead of selecting another application (reports/recovery-hardware-routes.md section 5). No decoded writer sets the selector: strap-read-safety.md section 3 finds no store to 0xfff89014 in any artifact and no access to 0xfff98000 outside the ROM, whose store preserves bits 2:0; a movw/movt pass over the ROM, both records, both loaders, images 4 and 5 and the plain image materializes 0xfff98000 nowhere and 0xfff89014 only as the port-mirror loop base (boot-40048.bin 0x2688, boot-50048.bin 0x22b8, id5-00bf1a00.bin 0x2d63ac), and the ROM rewrites 0xfff89008 before every sample. Blind spots stay open: register-indirect and table-driven writers and the image-4 ten-word MMIO base table at 0x829144 (holding 0xfff89000 and 0xfff98000) without an established consumer.
scope: XM1-body-01 official 1.50; the captured 16 KiB boot-ROM artifact, both boot records, both loaders, decoded images 4 and 5, the plain image and the existing reviewed captures. Host-only: no camera or USB access, no card written, no payload executed.
limitations: Both selector-writer checks are bounded negative evidence: the strap census omits register-offset, base-through-memory and table-driven forms, and the movw/movt pass sees only movw/movt pairs, so literal-pool constants and indirect writers are not excluded.
The electrical source and the warm-reset retention of 0xfff89014 bits 11:10 and 0xfff98000 bits 2:0 are unproved; SELECTOR-WRITE-01 and RESET-RETENTION-01 stay open.
No hardware test was run: no card written, no payload executed, no camera or USB access.

limitations: Their capture bytes were not fetched, so the comparison is by recorded content hash rather than a byte diff; a diff would add nothing to equal SHA-256 over equal lengths.
Content identity of a mask ROM is not a die identity, a revision identity or any statement about the application side or the peripherals.

claim: Block-by-block comparison of the X70 emulator's hardware models (X70-reported) against our own body's bytes, for the blocks the previous full-system assessment named (reports/x70-emulator-reference.md section 3.2). Our side is a fresh constant-address access scan with private-data/analysis/x-m1-1.50/bootrom/strap-scan.c over our ROM, both boot records, both loaders, images 4 and 5 and the plain image for ranges 0xfffb3000, 0xfffb4000, 0xfff01000, 0xfff91000 and 0xfff52000, plus the decodes in reports/bootrom-window.md and reports/firmware-extraction.md; the scanner decodes movw/movt, mov/mvn and pc-relative literal bases with immediate offsets and skips register-offset, post-indexed and table-driven forms, so the census is a lower bound. Readings: clock 0xfff88000 agrees (their ready bits 28-request to 24-ready and the +0x80 bit 16 status with our ROM's waits at 0xfff88080 bit 16, 0xfff88038 bit 28 to bit 24, and 0xfff88084 bit 0 on the halt path); GPIO 0xfff89000 agrees on the 0x40-stride port layout and on port 0 bits 11:10 as the boot source, which their boot fixture also sets; system 0xfff98000 agrees on the same five offsets {0,8,0x100,0x104,0x208}; DRAM 0xfff99000 is their DRAM controller and our unidentified block, with our config writes at +0x04..+0xf8, polls at +0x04/+0x08 and read-modify-write at +0x1c inside their offset set; reset 0xfffb2000 agrees on the same five offsets {4,8,0xc,0x10,0x14} that our ROM's every-boot pair writes hit; PHY 0xfff01000 agrees on the start bit at +0x00 and ready at +0x90 bit 28 and on the 0x248-wide register window our ROM indexes, so that base is not an interrupt controller; the two interrupt banks at 0xfffb3000/0xfffb4000 accept our ROM's conditional config words at +0x8c/+0xac/+0x10c/+0x12c/+0x15c, both records' +0xc00 writes, boot record 1's bit-24 writes to bank-1 +0x8c/+0xac/+0xcc/+0xec and image 5's enable read-modify-writes at +0x80..+0x8c/+0xa0..+0xac; timers 0xfff91000 agree on the register triple 0/4/8 that both records, both loaders and image 4 use, with our reload 30000, the counter/1875 tick measured at 99.88 Hz and the callback id 32 against their inferred power-of-two divider 1<<((control>>4)&7) and unmeasured physical source; the decompressor 0xfff43000 agrees on start +0x04, source +0x40, length +0x44, destination +0x48, read-only output count +0x4c, acknowledge +0x88, 16 KiB job pages and the 20-byte stream header before the token stream our decoder also skips; the media controller 0xfff52000/0xfff52800 agrees on type-1 geometry (2 KiB page, 64 pages per 128 KiB block), the 512-byte aperture at +0x400 whose first 16 bytes their program model fills from registers 0x40-0x4c (a candidate reading for our spare-prefix question and the unnamed +0x404 accept field), done and acknowledge at +0x54, and the DMA words +0xa0 (tag 0x401000), +0xa4 and +0xa8. Their 0xfff02000 fill/copy model supplies a register set where our assessment listed the map as missing. Coverage gaps that are not conflicts: our interrupt-bank reads at offsets 0x00..0x0c sit outside the families their model accepts, and each X70 model's register set is its own firmware's observed accesses. Classification: no evidence of a different chip, no evidence either way on revision, and the remaining differences are the same chip used by different firmware with different peripherals and a config block that skips the 0xfffb3000 sequence on our body (field +0x54 = 0x001a0000).

limitations: The census covers constant-address instruction forms only; register-offset, post-indexed and table-driven accesses are outside it, so each our-bytes finding is a lower bound.

claim: Four sibling-derived readings that correct or extend labels in our own reports, each unproved on our body until our own kernel decode or a capture settles it (reports/x70-emulator-reference.md section 3.2). (1) 0xfff01000 is a PHY-class block, not the interrupt controller: our ROM writes bit 0 to +0x00, writes 146 indexed words over +0x00..+0x248 and then waits unbounded on 0xfff01090 bit 28, and the state snapshot in image 5 at 0xed43dc reads bank offsets through 0x306c; the X70 model's only semantics for that base are a start bit at +0x00 and a ready bit at +0x90 bit 28. The 0xfff01000 line in reports/full-system-emulation.md section 2 and the 0xfff01000 row of reports/bootrom-window.md section 4 read as a PHY-class block instead. (2) The two 128-source interrupt-controller banks are 0xfffb3000 and 0xfffb4000: our ROM's conditional config words at +0x8c/+0xac/+0x10c/+0x12c/+0x15c, both records' writes to +0xc00 in both banks, boot record 1's bit-24 writes to bank-1 +0x8c/+0xac/+0xcc/+0xec at sites 0x1ec4-0x1ed0 and image 5's enable read-modify-writes at +0x80..+0x8c and +0xa0..+0xac all land inside the families the X70 model defines for these bases, where reports/bootrom-window.md section 4 currently records the 0xfffb3000 block as unidentified. (3) The same record 1 write of 0x01000000 to bank-1 +0xcc is the second core's release: it is the register and value the X70 board watches to start CPU1 after its high vectors are copied, which matches our own assessment's finding that the second CPU's side of the boot rendezvous is small and scripted. (4) The 0x3fff00xx exception-vector literals in boot record 2, unexplained in reports/update-validation-and-boot.md, name the second core's high-vector region at 0x3fff0000 in the X70 board's CPU1 handling.

The constant-address census that produced the supporting accesses skips register-offset, post-indexed and table-driven forms, so an image-side use may exist that the scan did not report.

claim: The X-M1 1.50 first and second boot records' execution order is byte-read from our own decode, and it fixes the T1 stop and the second core's release (reports/full-system-emulation.md sections 3 and 7). Record 1 (payload 0x40048, base 0, reset 0x1800; decode/ghidra/boot-40048.c FUN_00001800): sets 0x40020000 and 0x40020004 to 0x22b; copies 0x3e8 bytes from RAM 0x10000 to 0x7fff0000, the alias of physical 0x3fff0000; writes 0x01000000 to 0xfffb408c, 0xfffb40cc, 0xfffb40ac and 0xfffb40ec; initializes storage (FUN_00002034), builds the block skip list (FUN_00002058, 0x4804 = 0x4310), reads the segment table from media 0x140000 to 0x61c000 (FUN_00001dc4), publishes 0x4310 into 0x61c188, checks the trailer halfword at 0x24a0000 + 0x1e for 0xaaaa (FUN_00001cc0), copies loader records id 0/1 (FUN_0000231c) and decompresses image 4 with its bss fill (FUN_00002250, the fill over 0x89ec00 + 0x352e00 and then the engine to 0x61c400); FUN_00001d08 stores the loader record's header word at +0xc (0x40020) into RAM 0x4300 and *(0x61c40c) into 0x4304; the path clears 0x400a00c4, clears its own sync cell, waits for 0x40020004 to leave 0x22b, and the reset path's final transfer goes through 0x4300/0x4304 after the supervisor switch at 0x183c. Record 2 (payload 0x50048, base 0x10000, reset 0x11800; boot-50048-10000.c FUN_00011cc0): reads the boot-reason sample from companion register 0x6000 into 0x400a00c0, reads 16 one-byte companion values from 0x5000..0x5f00 into 0x400a00d0..0x400a00df and validates them (byte 14 = 0xaa, byte 15 = minus the sum of the first 15 bytes), writes 0x40020004 = 0, waits for 0x40020000 to leave 0x22b, and looks up shared segment id 1 for its handoff through 0x14c80/0x14c84.
